changes.comment: Code organization refactor stage 6a item 2a: renamed the class service/agent/service.ts's TeammateService -> AgentService and service/agent/runtime-generation.ts's TeammateRuntimeOwner -> RuntimeGeneration (propagated to every consumer's type-only imports across the package, e.g. dispatcher-service/ and team-service/; service/agent/factory.ts is left on the old name, since converting it into the per-dispatcher AgentServiceFactory is stage 6a item 2b). This one class now serves three roles (the Dispatcher's own Agent, a Team's leader, and an ordinary TeamMate) but hardcoded 'TeamMate' in every thrown-error message regardless of which role it was closing, locking, or starting; a Team's leader.close() (dissolve) or a Dispatcher agent's runtime-generation failure produced a wrong 'TeamMate ...' message. Added agentRoleNoun(role, name) (service/agent/service-types.ts, to avoid a service.ts <-> runtime-generation.ts import cycle) and used it at every such error message in these two files, so a Dispatcher agent now reads 'the Dispatcher agent ...' and a Team's leader reads 'Team leader "<name>" ...'. Most of an ordinary TeamMate's own wording is unchanged (byte-identical, same JSON.stringify(name) quoting); four messages that previously named 'TeamMate' without the entity's name now include it for every role, including teammate, as a byproduct of routing through the one shared helper: the close-note validation message (this is also a real fix, not just wording -- close() runs on a Team's leader too on dissolve, per team-service/closing.ts, so the pre-existing text was already wrong there), the two closed-with-no-closed_at invariant-violation messages, and the stale-lock-token invariant-violation message. Also deleted two dead-by-construction fields: ownsWorktreeOnClose (its condition, restricted to the three real construction sites, was already exactly implied by identity.worktree.mode === 'managed' && identity.worktree.cleanup === 'delete-on-close' alone -- the Dispatcher agent and every Team leader are always worktree.mode 'reuse-cwd', and a Team-scoped TeamMate's spawn path always forces a reuse-cwd shared workspace, so the flag never disagreed with the identity's own facts since it was introduced) and assertIdentityScope plus runtime-id.ts's three assert*Scope helper functions (the identity was already read by a store scoped to the correct directory by the owner that materialized it, so re-checking scope on every ensureStarted() call had no failure scenario construction-time scoping doesn't already rule out). No persisted format, public API, or MCP/Command contract changed.
